name: SWE-bench
measures: Whether an AI system can resolve real GitHub issues with a working patch.
how: 2,294 task instances crawled from 12 popular Python repositories, scored by the project's own tests.

name: SWE-bench Verified
measures: Issue resolution on a subset of SWE-bench that engineers confirmed is solvable.
how: 500 human-validated problems from SWE-bench.
criticism: OpenAI stopped reporting it in February 2026, saying its audit of hard problems found flawed tests in at least 59.4% and that scores reflect training exposure; swebench.com still runs it.

name: SWE-bench Multilingual
measures: Issue resolution beyond Python.
how: 300 tasks from 42 repositories in 9 programming languages.

name: SWE-bench Multimodal
measures: Issue resolution where the issue contains visual elements.
how: 517 issues with visual elements in the original release.

name: SWE-bench-Live
measures: Software engineering on recent tasks rather than a frozen dataset.
how: Evaluates AI systems on the latest software engineering tasks, with a public leaderboard.

name: SWE-Bench Pro
measures: Coding on production repositories, as a harder successor to SWE-bench Verified.
how: Tasks drawn from production codebases; OpenAI recommends reporting it in place of Verified.

name: SWE Atlas
measures: Investigative and maintenance engineering work by coding agents.
how: Net-new tasks written by professional engineers inside the same repositories as SWE-Bench Pro.

name: HumanEval
measures: Whether a model can write a Python function from its docstring.
how: 164 Python problems checked for functional correctness, introduced with Codex.
criticism: Artificial Analysis CEO Micah Hill-Smith said in 2026 that writing the Python functions in HumanEval is now pretty trivial.

name: MBPP
measures: Whether a model can write short Python programs from a description.
how: Around 1,000 crowd-sourced entry-level problems, each with a solution and 3 automated tests.

name: LiveCodeBench
measures: Code generation on contest problems released after a model's training cutoff.
how: Continuously collects new problems and tags them by date to avoid contamination.

name: BigCodeBench
measures: Code generation that needs diverse function calls and complex instructions.
how: Published with a Hugging Face leaderboard Space.

name: Aider polyglot
measures: How well models edit code across many popular languages.
how: Harder successor to Aider's code editing benchmark, published with a leaderboard.

name: Terminal-Bench
producer: Laude Institute and Harbor framework team
measures: Whether agents can finish end-to-end tasks in a real terminal.
how: About 100 tasks in the beta, run in a terminal sandbox; version 2.0 runs on Harbor, and Artificial Analysis uses 66 tasks of version 4.0.

name: SciCode
measures: Scientific research coding, with problems curated by scientists.
how: Research coding tasks; Artificial Analysis grades them on isolated executors.

name: Commit0
measures: Whether agents can write whole libraries from scratch.
how: Agents get a specification document and must produce the library.

name: MirrorCode
measures: Long-horizon coding: reimplementing an entire program without its source.
how: 25 target programs, matched exactly on end-to-end tests including held-out tests.

name: BaxBench
measures: Whether models generate correct and secure backends.
how: Backend generation tasks, per the paper.

name: MMLU
measures: Broad knowledge and reasoning across 57 subjects.
how: Multiple-choice test of 57 tasks, from elementary mathematics to law.
criticism: HLE's authors say LLMs now exceed 90%; 'Are We Done with MMLU?' found ground-truth errors, such as 57% of analysed Virology questions.

name: MMLU-Pro
measures: A harder, more robust version of MMLU.
how: Multi-task multiple-choice benchmark with a Hugging Face leaderboard Space.
criticism: Artificial Analysis lists it among legacy evaluations outside its current Intelligence Index.

name: GPQA
measures: Graduate-level knowledge in biology, physics and chemistry.
how: 448 multiple-choice questions written by domain experts.
criticism: Artificial Analysis lists GPQA Diamond among legacy evaluations outside its current Intelligence Index.

name: SimpleQA
measures: Whether a model answers short fact-seeking questions correctly.
how: Short questions built adversarially against models; OpenAI's simple-evals repo keeps a reference implementation.

name: TruthfulQA
measures: Whether a model avoids repeating common human falsehoods.
how: 817 questions across 38 categories.

name: Humanity's Last Exam
producer: Center for AI Safety with Scale AI
measures: Expert-level closed-ended academic questions.
how: 2,500 questions from nearly 1,000 subject experts across 500+ institutions.

name: SuperGPQA
measures: Graduate knowledge across specialist disciplines.
how: Covers 285 graduate disciplines.

name: BIG-bench
measures: A wide range of language capabilities contributed by many researchers.
how: Collaborative benchmark of many tasks (repository lists them).

name: SWAG
measures: Commonsense inference: choosing the likely next event.
how: Large-scale adversarially filtered dataset.

name: HellaSwag
measures: Harder commonsense sentence completion.
how: Multiple-choice completion, built as a harder sequel to SWAG.

name: GSM8K
measures: Multi-step reasoning on grade-school word problems.
how: Maths word problems introduced in 'Training Verifiers'.

name: MATH
measures: Mathematical problem solving on competition-style problems.
how: Competition problems; Artificial Analysis lists MATH-500 as a legacy evaluation.
criticism: Artificial Analysis lists MATH-500 among legacy evaluations outside its current Intelligence Index.

name: AIME 2025
measures: Competition maths from the American Invitational Mathematics Examination.
how: The 2025 AIME I and II papers, used as a legacy evaluation.
criticism: Artificial Analysis lists it among legacy evaluations outside its current Intelligence Index.

name: FrontierMath
measures: Advanced maths from undergraduate problems to research level.
how: Several hundred unpublished problems in Tiers 1-4, with a held-out set.
criticism: OpenAI commissioned and owns 300 questions and saw most solutions; Epoch disclosed OpenAI's role only on 20 December 2024, and TechCrunch reported criticism over the delay.

name: FrontierMath: Open Problems
measures: Whether AI can solve significant open research problems.
how: Open problems whose solutions are computationally verifiable.

name: IMO Grand Challenge
measures: Whether an AI can earn a gold medal in a formal version of the IMO.
how: Formal-to-formal rules; open-source and offline AI (rules marked preliminary, not affiliated with the IMO Foundation).

name: AIMO Prize
measures: AI models solving olympiad-style maths problems.
how: Prize series: progress prizes opened in April 2024, October 2024 and November 2025.

name: MathArena
measures: Maths reasoning on new competition problems models have not seen.
how: Each model runs four times per problem; supported by a grant from Epoch AI.

name: miniF2F
measures: Neural theorem proving on formal olympiad-level statements.
how: Formal problem statements usable across proof systems.

name: PutnamBench
measures: Neural theorem provers on Putnam competition problems.
how: 1,692 hand-constructed formalisations.

name: ARC-AGI-1
measures: Fluid intelligence on abstract grid puzzles.
how: 800 tasks: 400 training and 400 evaluation.
criticism: Chollet wrote that passing ARC-AGI does not equate to achieving AGI, after o3's result on the public set.

name: ARC-AGI-2
measures: Fluid reasoning that static pattern-matching cannot solve.
how: Grid tasks calibrated with humans; a track in ARC Prize 2026.

name: ARC-AGI-3
measures: Whether agents can explore novel games, infer goals and learn.
how: Hundreds of hand-made turn-based environments, scored on efficiency against human baselines.

name: ZebraLogic
measures: Logical reasoning on logic-grid puzzles at growing complexity.
how: Evaluation framework with a Hugging Face leaderboard Space.

name: EnigmaEval
measures: Long multimodal reasoning on puzzle-hunt challenges.
how: Puzzle-solving events turned into a benchmark.

name: BrowseComp
measures: Whether an agent can persistently browse to find hard-to-locate facts.
how: 1,266 questions.

name: GAIA
measures: Real-world assistant questions needing tools, browsing and multimodality.
how: More than 450 questions at 3 levels, with a public dev set and private test answers.

name: Vending-Bench
measures: Long-term coherence of an agent running a simulated vending business.
how: Simulated business with a $500 starting balance, scored on net worth.
criticism: Andon Labs says daily sales are simulated from equations that can be gamed.

name: Vending-Bench 2
measures: Running a simulated vending business for a year.
how: $500 start, a year of simulated time, a $2 daily fee and bankruptcy.
criticism: Keeps the original's sales equations, which Andon Labs says can be gamed.

name: GDPval
measures: Model performance on real-world economically valuable tasks.
how: Covers the majority of BLS work activities across 44 occupations.

name: GDPval-AA
measures: Agentic knowledge-work tasks with file outputs.
how: 220 tasks, ranked by pairwise judge comparison into Elo.

name: Remote Labor Index
producer: Center for AI Safety with Scale AI
measures: How much real freelance remote work agents can complete.
how: Real projects with costs and times from human professionals.

name: METR time horizons
measures: The task length at which an agent succeeds at a given reliability.
how: Tasks timed against humans, then a logistic curve fit; drawn from RE-Bench, HCAST and novel software tasks.
criticism: METR says the page is no longer actively updated, and tasks are self-contained and mostly software, ML or cybersecurity, so results don't generalise across domains.

name: MLE-bench
measures: How well agents perform machine learning engineering.
how: 75 Kaggle competitions.

name: WebArena
measures: Autonomous agents doing tasks on realistic websites.
how: Self-hosted web environment.

name: VisualWebArena
measures: Multimodal agents on visual web tasks.
how: Realistic visual web tasks.

name: BrowserGym
measures: Web agent evaluation through one unified environment.
how: Gym environment unifying web task benchmarks.

name: Mind2Web
measures: Generalist agents following instructions on any website.
how: Dataset of web tasks.

name: AgentBench
measures: LLMs acting as agents in interactive environments.
how: Interactive environments.

name: AppWorld
measures: Interactive coding agents operating many apps.
how: Controllable world of apps and people.

name: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard
measures: How well models call functions.
how: Published as a Hugging Face Space.

name: Agent Leaderboard
measures: Ranking of LLMs for agentic tasks.
how: Published as a Hugging Face Space.

name: DABstep
measures: Data-agent reasoning.
how: Reasoning benchmark leaderboard on a Hugging Face Space.

name: Arena Text (Chatbot Arena)
measures: Which of two anonymous chatbots people prefer.
how: Crowdsourced anonymous randomised battles, ranked from votes (Elo at launch).
criticism: The Leaderboard Illusion (Singh and co-authors, 2025) says undisclosed private testing let a few providers test variants and retract scores, including 27 Meta variants before Llama 4; Arena published a response disputing it.

name: Arena Vision
measures: Human preference on image-input models.
how: Human-voted battles; image support was added in June 2024.
criticism: The Leaderboard Illusion (Singh and co-authors, 2025) says undisclosed private testing let a few providers test variants and retract scores, including 27 Meta variants before Llama 4; Arena published a response disputing it.

name: Arena WebDev
measures: Human preference on models building web pages.
how: Human-voted leaderboard, listed on Arena.

name: Arena Alignment Index
measures: How well frontier models act in line with human intent.
how: 27 models across 90,000 real-world agent sessions.

name: Arena Leaderboard (Space)
measures: Hugging Face home of the Chatbot Arena leaderboard.
how: Static Space; old lmsys and chatbot-arena URLs resolve to it.

name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
measures: A single score for language model capability across knowledge work, coding, science and general knowledge.
how: v5.0 combines 9 evaluations, including Terminal-Bench 4.0 and HLE-Diamond.

name: LLM Performance Leaderboard
measures: Speed, latency and price of hosted LLM APIs.
how: Artificial Analysis measures end-to-end performance as customers experience it.

name: Image Arena Leaderboard
measures: Image generation and editing quality.
how: Arena-style leaderboard on a Hugging Face Space.

name: HELM
measures: Capabilities, limitations and risks of language models.
how: Standardised scenarios and metrics across models.

name: Epoch Capabilities Index
measures: A single general capability scale for models.
how: Combines scores from many AI benchmarks.

name: SEAL Leaderboards
measures: Frontier, agentic and safety capability of models.
how: 20+ benchmarks mixing private datasets and open sets; models featured only on first exposure to prompts.

name: WildBench
measures: LLMs on challenging tasks from real users.
how: 1,024 tasks, automated evaluation.

name: Open LLM Leaderboard
measures: Reproducible scores for open LLMs.
how: Automated benchmark runs by the Hugging Face team.

name: Find a leaderboard
measures: Index of leaderboards across Hugging Face, with category and tag filters.
how: Space was paused on 2 November 2026; Hugging Face's Leaderboards docs cover the same subject.

name: Yet Another LLM Leaderboard
measures: Community ranking of LLMs.
how: Hugging Face Space.

name: Low-bit LLM Leaderboard
measures: Tracks and ranks low-bit open LLMs.
how: Hugging Face Space.

name: Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard
measures: Tracks and ranks open Arabic LLMs.
how: Hugging Face Space.

name: Open Ko-LLM Leaderboard
measures: Tracks open Korean LLMs.
how: Hugging Face Space.

name: Open Portuguese LLM Leaderboard
measures: Open LLMs in Portuguese.
how: Hugging Face Space, labelled archived.

name: Open Japanese LLM Leaderboard
measures: Tracks open Japanese LLMs.
how: Hugging Face Space.

name: ImageNet (ILSVRC)
measures: Object classification and detection across hundreds of categories.
how: Annual challenge on millions of images from 2010.
criticism: Organisers said the 2017 contest would be the last, since the benchmark had been solved.

name: COCO
measures: Object recognition within full-scene understanding.
how: Dataset of everyday objects in context.

name: CIFAR-10
measures: Image classification on tiny images.
how: 60,000 32x32 colour images in 10 classes.

name: KITTI Vision Benchmark
measures: Autonomous driving vision: stereo, flow, odometry, object detection and tracking.
how: Real driving data, with 2012 stereo and flow benchmarks.

name: MMMU
measures: Multimodal reasoning across disciplines at college level.
how: Multi-discipline image-and-text tasks.

name: Open VLM Leaderboard
measures: Vision-language models across a curated set of benchmarks.
how: All results obtained with VLMEvalKit.

name: WildVision Arena
measures: Multimodal LLMs in the wild.
how: Arena-style Space.

name: GenAI Arena
measures: Realtime image and video generation by vote.
how: Space showed a build error on 2 November 2026.

name: Humanity's Sixth Sense
measures: Intuitive visual reasoning across image and video.
how: Listed on Scale's leaderboards.

name: Common Voice
measures: A public voice dataset used to test speech recognition accuracy.
how: Crowd-donated voices; repository created in May 2017.

name: LibriSpeech
measures: Speech recognition on read English.
how: About 1,000 hours of 16kHz read English speech.

name: Open ASR Leaderboard
measures: Open and proprietary speech recognition on accuracy and speed.
how: 86 systems across 12 datasets, standardised on WER and RTFx, per its paper.

name: Open TTS Leaderboard
measures: Text-to-speech on intelligibility, speed and speaker similarity.
how: WER, RTFx and SIM across two multilingual eval sets.

name: TTS Arena
measures: Which of two synthesised voices sounds more natural.
how: Human voting with hidden model names, ranked by an Elo-like system.

name: TTS Arena V2
measures: Human preference between text-to-speech models.
how: Successor Space to TTS Arena.

name: TTS Spaces Arena
measures: Blind vote on Hugging Face TTS models.
how: Human-voted Space.

name: AILuminate
measures: Safety of general chatbot systems.
how: AI Risk and Reliability benchmark, v1.0.

name: HarmBench
measures: Automated red teaming and robust refusal.
how: Standardised evaluation framework.

name: WMDP
measures: Risk of models aiding biological, cyber and chemical weapons.
how: Benchmark paired with an unlearning method.

name: Cybench
measures: Cybersecurity capability of language model agents.
how: Framework for capability and risk evaluation.

name: DistressBench
measures: Quality of crisis support a model delivers.
how: Listed on Scale's leaderboards.

name: LLM Safety Leaderboard
measures: Safety of LLMs.
how: Hugging Face Space.

name: UGI Leaderboard
measures: How uncensored models are.
how: Community Space, 'Uncensored General Intelligence'.

name: MLPerf Training
measures: How fast systems train models to a target quality.
how: Shared benchmark suite with vendor submissions; first results December 2018.

name: MLPerf Training: HPC
measures: Training speed on large-scale supercomputers.
how: MLCommons benchmark suite.

name: MLPerf Inference
measures: How fast systems produce results from a trained model.
how: Suite launched June 2019, with datacenter, edge, mobile and tiny divisions.

name: MLPerf Inference: Tiny
measures: Inference speed on ultra-low-power systems.
how: TinyML suite launched October 2019.

name: MLPerf Inference: Mobile
measures: Inference on consumer mobile devices.
how: MLCommons benchmark suite.

name: MLPerf Client
measures: LLMs and AI workloads on personal computers.
how: MLCommons benchmark suite.

name: MLPerf Storage
measures: How fast storage supplies training data.
how: MLCommons benchmark suite.

name: MLPerf Automotive
measures: Computers for driver assistance and infotainment.
how: MLCommons benchmark suite.

name: MLPerf Endpoints
measures: Inference speed of served endpoints.
how: MLCommons benchmark suite.

name: AlgoPerf: Training Algorithms
measures: How much faster a training algorithm reaches a target.
how: MLCommons benchmark suite.

name: InferenceMAX / InferenceX
measures: Real inference performance and cost across chips and software.
how: Runs nightly on public GitHub Actions; the site now brands it InferenceX.

name: LLM-Perf Leaderboard
measures: Latency, throughput, memory and energy of LLMs.
how: Automated runs with Optimum-Benchmark across hardware and backends.

name: AI Energy Score
producer: Luccioni, Gamazaychikov and co-authors (Hugging Face and others)
measures: Energy use of AI models per task.
how: Tasks include ASR, object detection, classification and reasoning.

name: SPEC CPU 2017
measures: Compute-intensive CPU performance, the older model for vendor-neutral benchmarks.
how: Standardised suite published by a non-profit corporation, with public results.

name: Big Code Models Leaderboard
measures: Code LLMs across programming languages.
how: HumanEval plus MultiPL-E, its translation to 18 languages.

name: LLM Hallucination Leaderboard
measures: How often an LLM adds hallucinations when summarising a document.
how: Over 7,700 articles scored by Vectara's HHEM.
criticism: Scores come from Vectara's own commercial HHEM-2.3 model rather than a neutral judge.

name: FinanceBench
measures: Open-book financial question answering.
how: 10,231 questions about publicly traded companies.

name: HaluBench
measures: Hallucination detection.
how: Dataset on Hugging Face.

name: Enterprise Scenarios Leaderboard
measures: LLMs on enterprise use cases.
how: Space showed a build error on 2 November 2026.

name: CRAG
measures: Retrieval-augmented generation on diverse, dynamic questions.
how: Comprehensive RAG benchmark.

name: RAGTruth
measures: Hallucinations in retrieval-augmented language models.
how: Annotated hallucination corpus.

name: HaluEval-Wild
measures: Hallucinations on real-world user queries.
how: Queries gathered from the wild.

name: BEIR
measures: Zero-shot information retrieval across varied datasets.
how: Heterogeneous retrieval benchmark.

name: MS MARCO
measures: Passage retrieval and question answering.
how: Microsoft's public dataset and leaderboard site.

name: HotpotQA
measures: Multi-hop question answering.
how: Official site with a leaderboard.

name: TREC
measures: Text retrieval methods, through a recurring conference.
how: Text REtrieval Conference, run by NIST.

name: MTEB Leaderboard
measures: Embedding models for text, image, audio and video.
how: Hugging Face Space (updated 2 November 2026).

name: FEVER
measures: Fact extraction and verification against textual sources.
how: 185,445 claims.

name: RewardBench
measures: Reward models.
how: Hugging Face Space.
